chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding the one in Ihram who catches the prey, makes it bleed, then releases it: 'Upon him is its penalty.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.جَزَاء: Penalty or compensation (specifically damm in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a person in Ihram who catches game and releases it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes that the penalty of damm (compensation) is obligatory even if the hunted animal is released alive after being wounded, emphasizing that the act of hunting itself triggers the liability. It highlights the juristic principle that the validity of the penalty does not depend on the retention of the prey, a key distinction in Shia fiqh regarding the conditions of Ihram. The narration underscores the seriousness of violating the sanctity of the pilgrimage state, regardless of the animal's ultimate fate.
